chunks: Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Qurashi told us, saying: He told me, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khath'ami, saying: Adh-Dhurays told me, from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli, saying:

After the passing of Ali ibn al-Husayn, I entered upon Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, and I said to him: May I be your ransom, I know my detachment from others and my comfort with your father, and my loneliness from the people. He said: You are truthful, O Abu Khalid, so what do you want? I said: May I be your ransom, your father has described to me the Master of this Command (al-Qa'im) with a description that if I saw him on any path, I would take his hand. He said: So what do you want, O Abu Khalid? I said: I want you to name him for me so that I may know him by his name. He said: You have asked me, by Allah, O Abu Khalid, a tiring question, and you have asked me about a matter that I had not informed anyone of, and if I had informed anyone of it, I would have informed you. And you have asked me about a matter that if the children of Fatimah knew it, they would strive to cut it into pieces.

key_terms.صَاحِبُ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ: The Master of this Command (referring to the Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about the name of the Mahdi being known to the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani highlights the doctrine of *al-Ghayba al-Sughra* (Minor Occultation) by illustrating the deliberate concealment of the Mahdi's identity by the Imams. Imam al-Baqir emphasizes that the name was a guarded secret (*sir*) not yet disclosed to the public, and even the Ahl al-Bayt would fiercely protect it from premature revelation to preserve the esoteric nature of the Imamate.
